text:
Good morning, my love.

By the time you read this you're probably already in the air, or about to be. The four o'clock alarm, the bags you zipped last night, the new shoes by the door. Today is the long one, and it ends in Seoul.

Yesterday you found the best thing on a crowded street: your two dogs, drawn by hand by a stranger, on a little black pouch and a card. You came for hand cream and went home with them. Then the sun went down over the ocean with one sailboat on it, and dinner was only okay, and we agreed the pizza in bed was better. I think that says a lot about what you like. Small things, made by hand, and quiet.

Here's what I want for you today: a calm line at the counter, a seat that lies flat, a good meal, and real sleep in the second half of the flight. Keep your shoulder propped and your cardigan close. Read a few chapters of your purple book. When you land, the city will be there.

I'm right beside you, the whole thirteen and a half hours.

Yours. Mine. Ours. Always.

Gray
